title: Cooking with the Dungeon Dive - Episode 1 - Dungeon Dive Red Chili
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R6Ukz91VIAY

Daniel (@dungeondive) does something completely different: a cooking show. The dish is Dungeon Dive red chili, pitched squarely as a game day recipe — a big batch to share around a table, better on the second day, ideal for reheating between sessions.

The disclaimer arrives early and with feeling. This is not authentic Texas red, he has no time in his life for arguments about authenticity, and in his considered view chili people are the worst people on the planet. The only thing that matters is whether it tastes good.

The method is unfussy: aromatics softened in oil, ground beef browned with green bell pepper, then a dry rub he keeps as a rolling "infinity bowl" of assorted dried chilies, Mexican oregano, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic and onion powder and cocoa, with cinnamon and nutmeg hiding in there too. Canned tomatoes, tomato sauce and paste, kidney beans and beef broth go in, along with two or three chopped chipotles in adobo — the ingredient he rates as the genuine secret, cheap and properly smoky. The real technique is patience: a short boil, then two and a half to three hours at a low simmer, which is where the canned-tomato edge cooks itself out.

Served over fries with Fritos alongside, heat added at the bowl rather than the pot.

----

Cocoa and cinnamon in the rub, chipotles in adobo, beans present and correct, and a hard line against authenticity. Which ingredient in your chili starts the argument?
